Who Should Run a Region When Nobody Was Elected?

By Furaihan Kamyl Arnazaye · 2023 · 3 min read
Key takeaways
  • 272 regions, about half of Indonesia's provinces, regencies, and cities, were led by appointed acting heads before the 2024 elections.
  • Against the 2020 Indonesia Democracy Index, appointment fits only 2 of 34 provinces: Sumatra Utara and Sulawesi Selatan.
  • 27 provinces fit indirect election through the DPRD, and 5 fit direct election.
  • In practice, the policy brings weak legitimacy, scattered legal authority, and doubts about neutrality.
  • The recommendations are one legal basis that lists what an acting head may do, and transparency in every appointment.

Between 2022 and 2024, a large part of Indonesia was run by regional heads nobody voted for. Regional elections were moved to 2024 so they could be held together with the national election. Governors, regents, and mayors whose terms ended in 2022 and 2023 were replaced by acting regional heads, penjabat kepala daerah (PKD), appointed by the Minister of Home Affairs from senior civil servants.

101 regions had a PKD in 2022. By the end of 2023, another 171 were expected. In total, 272 regions, about half of all provinces, regencies, and cities, were led by an appointed official.

There are two ways to see this. From a technocratic view, senior civil servants know how government works, so appointing them keeps services running. From a democratic view, a political office is being filled without the people who are supposed to choose it. Earlier studies had called the policy ineffective, but mostly on normative grounds. We wanted a test that did not rest on opinion alone.

Matching the mechanism to each province

Mahardika and Fatayati (2020) offer a way to decide how a region should choose its head based on its democratic maturity. It uses the three aspects of the Indonesia Democracy Index (IDI): civil liberties, political rights, and democratic institutions. Each province falls into one of three categories, and each category suggests a different mechanism.

CategoryRuleSuggested mechanism
1All three aspects below the national averageAppointment, as with PKD
2Some aspects above, some belowIndirect election through the DPRD
3All three aspects above the national averageDirect regional election

Appointment, the way PKD are chosen, only fits the first category. So the test is simple. Place every province against the national average on all three aspects, and count how many land in the first category.

Key findingOnly 2 of 34 provinces fit appointment: Sumatra Utara and Sulawesi Selatan.

27 provinces fall in the mixed category, which suggests indirect election through the DPRD. 5 provinces are above the national average on all three aspects, which points to direct elections: DKI Jakarta, DI Yogyakarta, Kalimantan Timur, Kalimantan Barat, and Gorontalo.

The legal basis is Article 201 of Law No. 10 of 2016. Acting governors come from senior executive positions (JPT madya). Acting regents and mayors come from primary senior executive positions (JPT pratama). Under Permendagri No. 1 of 2018, the minister appoints acting regents and mayors on the governor's proposal, or without it in the national interest.

Three problems beyond the numbers

The index shows a mismatch. The normative analysis shows what that mismatch does in practice. We found three problems that leave social rights and political freedom unprotected.

Two recommendations

RecommendationWhat it involves
1. One legal basis for PKD authorityConsolidate the rules scattered across the regional government law, PP No. 49 of 2008, and Permendagri No. 74 of 2016 into one clear legal basis, with an explicit list of what a PKD may and may not do
2. Transparency in every appointmentPublish the profiles of candidates. Publish the assessment results against clear indicators. Open a reporting channel for integrity problems and abuse of power by PKD

The study has limits. It uses secondary data, the 2020 IDI, the latest available when we wrote it. The classification also rests on one framework for matching mechanisms to democratic maturity. A different framework could draw the lines elsewhere.

The PKD policy kept regional government running, and in 32 of 34 provinces it did so with a mechanism the province's democratic maturity does not call for.
